title_original: Elon Musk Has Invested in Skydance, David Ellison Confirms: ‘To Have Him as a Shareholder Is an Honor’

blocks.text: David Ellison , chairman and CEO of Skydance , confirmed that tech mogul Elon Musk has invested in the company, formed through the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

Musk, the world’s richest person, invested about $1 billion in Skydance post-merger, CNBC and Semafor reported last month. Ellison, speaking Wednesday at the New York Times’ 2026 DealBook Summit at Manhattan’s Jazz at Lincoln Center, acknowledged that Musk is a part-owner of Skydance but he did not confirm the investment amount.

blocks.text: The New York Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin asked Ellison about the reports of Musk investing a billion dollars into Skydance, “and I think some people wanted to know whether this is the beginning of something bigger with Starlink long-term, or is a one-off as a given his relationship with your father,” Larry Ellison.

Ellison responded, “So look, I have so much admiration and respect for Elon. I mean, I don’t know if you saw recently, but literally watching, you know, [SpaceX’s] Starship, it’s a marvel…. I mean, he is both the [Nikola] Tesla and [Thomas] Edison… He is, from my perspective, the greatest entrepreneur of our time, and he doesn’t invest in a lot of companies.”

Ellison continued, “So to have his vote of confidence and to have him as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege. And if there was any opportunity to be able to collaborate with him in the future… [which] is the appropriate opportunity in the future, we’d be thrilled to do so. But there’s nothing [right now].”

Sorkin asked Ellison whether he is still planning to put Alex Gibney’s documentary “Musk” — which prompted a legal threat from the tech titan against the filmmaker — on HBO. (“Musk” has been pegged to begin streaming on HBO Max in the first quarter of 2027.) Ellison responded, “Of course.”

blocks.text: Ellison’s Paramount Skydance closed its $111 billion megamerger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 , with major backing from his father, Oracle billionaire Larry Ellison. The company, one of the biggest media and entertainment conglomerates in the industry, has around $80 billion in net debt and is expected to lay off thousands of employees as part of achieving $6 billion in annualized savings by 2029.
